feature: A full-screen recording keeps up as it plays across a cut
summary: Playing a cut-down full-screen Retina recording no longer sticks at the cut. The far side of each cut, and the shot coming in over a dissolve, is read before the playhead gets there, so the picture arrives on time while the sound goes on.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open 'Full screen Retina recording 3456x2234.mp4' (Scripts/playtest/fixtures) and press Space to pause.
Move the playhead a quarter of the way in and press Command K, then to the middle and press Command K again.
Click the middle piece and press Delete.
Press Home, then Space, and watch the picture as the playhead crosses the cut.
Click the cut, pick Cross dissolve in the panel, press Home and play it again.
Cut your own five-minute recording down to a minute or two and play it through.

evaluate: Does the picture change at the cut at the same moment the sound does, with no freeze?
During the dissolve, do both shots move smoothly, with neither one stopping for a moment?
On a long recording with many cuts, does any cut still stick?
Does playing feel as smooth with cuts as it did before you cut anything?
rough: Before and after, same walk, same machine. Across a cut: before 3 of 20 looks late by up to 23 frames (the manager saw 4 of 20, up to 27); after 0 of 20 in seven runs in a row, and 0 of 20 with eight cores busy with other work.

Across a dissolve on that cut: before 6 of 20 looks late by up to 20 frames; after 0 of 20 in seven runs in a row, and under load. The check now also watches the incoming shot during a dissolve, which it did not before.

The far side of a cut is opened a second and a half ahead. A recording whose key frames are further apart than that, played with cuts closer together than that, could still be a frame or two late at a cut. Nothing has shown it yet.
Playing backwards with J still reads frame by frame and can lag on a full-screen recording; that is task playing-backwards-with-j-keeps-up-on-a-full-scre.
No mock covers this surface: nothing on screen changed, only how quickly frames arrive. Both pictures are the real window after playing to the end.
